title: Uploads: today's FTP path, the proposed presigned-S3 path, and the worker opened up
persona: A backend lead proposing to move file uploads off an FTP drop, showing what exists today, what is new and what goes away.
realism: Migration whiteboards mix today and the proposal on one board; people point at code ('that's the upload route') and blow one box up to show its insides.

steps.say: Today the app posts the whole file to our upload API.
It drops it on the FTP box, and a batch importer picks it up every five minutes.
That box is the upload route, this file.
The FTP drop and the importer are what goes away.
Instead the app asks the API for a presigned URL and puts the file straight into S3.
And an S3 event wakes a new upload worker.
Inside the worker it's three steps.
Scan, make the thumbnails, then write the metadata, and I'm not sure the metadata write belongs here.
So these two go away completely.

steps.note: worry: old app versions still POST the file, keep the route for a while?

steps.say: Old app versions are the risk.

story: Mobile app and Upload API exist today; FTP drop and Batch importer are going away; S3 (presigned), Upload worker and the arrows to them are the new, proposed path.
The Upload API box is the code in src/api/routes/upload.ts, and the Batch importer is src/jobs/batch_importer.rb.
The frame 'inside Upload worker' is what is inside the Upload worker: virus scan, then thumbnails (src/workers/thumbnail.ts), then write metadata.
They are unsure whether writing metadata belongs in the worker (it is dashed and they said so).
'These two go away completely' refers to the FTP drop and the Batch importer, which they pointed at.
Their worry: old app versions still POST the file, so the upload route may need to stay for a while.
partner_should_ask_about: what happens to uploads from old app versions during the switch
where metadata gets written if not in the worker
